Although less likely, breast cancer must be considered in the differential diagnosis, especially given the patient's age and the presence of a new, firm mass.
A lipoma is a possible diagnosis, as it can present as a firm, mobile mass in the breast tissue.
A breast cyst is another possible diagnosis, as it can present as a firm, tender mass, although the ultrasonography findings would be more characteristic of a solid lesion.

Pseudogynecomastia, which refers to the accumulation of fat in the breast tissue, is a possible diagnosis, although the patient's history of anabolic-steroid use and the presence of a firm mass make gynecomastia more likely.
